_doc: PW2 -- the AUTHORED half of the self-clearing-alarm census. The hits are DERIVED by background/self_clearing_alarm_census.py (writer set intersected with reader set per state path, over background/ and tools/); this file records the judgement on each. A hit with no row here, or a 'benign' row with no reason, makes `--check` exit 1 -- so a newly-written control of this shape lands RED instead of joining the class quietly. AND THE INVERSE, from 2026-09-05: a ROW whose hit has DISAPPEARED also makes `--check` exit 1 (`eroded_dispositions()`). Until then only 'a hit with no row' was checked, so a path that stopped being a hit needed no disposition and the gate stayed green while the class shrank -- measured at c30738d77, 17 rows had lost their subject and `undispositioned()` returned []. This row set is the census's HIGH-WATER MARK: authored, in git, derived from nothing, which is why checking today's derivation against it is not the read-your-own-output tautology a remembered hit count would be. Do not delete a row to make the gate green -- either the census went blind on the path (the finding) or the control was genuinely repaired, and only the second is admissible, in writing, via `declassified`. AND THE REGISTER'S OWN LOW-WATER MARK, from 2026-09-05: the sentence before this one -- 'do not delete a row to make the gate green' -- was prose with no falsifier, and every rung iterates either the hits or the rows, so a key in NEITHER was the subject of nothing. Deleting the row AND the hit together returned clean from all five rungs, measured on this file at 50 rows. Worse, since `eroded_dispositions()` REFUSES a row whose path the census can no longer resolve, deleting the row was the cure for its own refusal. `removed_dispositions()` now compares this file against its own copy at HEAD: a row that was here and is not here now makes `--check` exit 1 unless `_retired` says why. A carrier genuinely deleted from the tree is still removable -- in writing, and only in writing.

_verdicts.real: The path carries an EPISODE-SCOPED field -- an episode-start timestamp or a consecutive-failure counter -- that an alarm reads for SEVERITY, and a write that has not demonstrated the episode ended can shorten or reset it. Requires the append-or-monotonic guard (background/episode_monotonic.py).
_verdicts.benign: The path carries no episode-scoped field, so no write can shorten an episode. A latest-value watermark, a once-per-period guard, a seen-set, or an append-only log. The reason is mandatory.
_verdicts._scope_of_benign: BENIGN ANSWERS ONE QUESTION: can a write SHORTEN an episode? It is not a clean bill of health for the file. In particular it says nothing about whether the carrier's LOADER tells ABSENT from PRESENT-BUT-UNREADABLE -- a seen-set, a watermark or a read-modify-write store can be perfectly benign on the episode question and still destroy data, or crash, when its state file is corrupt. Rows swept for that carry a `loader` field saying what the answer is, and the sweep is ranked by what the carrier's WRITER does: a read-modify-write over the whole record can DESTROY the record on a corrupt read, where a pure reader only loses a suppression or spends a cycle. A row without one has not been asked, which is a gap and not a pass.
_verdicts._scope_of_resemblance: A REASON THAT DEFERS TO A SIBLING ROW IS AN UNOPENED ROW, AND IT READS AS ASKED-AND-ANSWERED (2026-09-05 delivery-seat re-audit). Eight rows closed on 'same shape as X' / 'same reasoning as X' / 'append-only' rather than on their carrier's own code. Re-opened against the code, SEVEN were wrong about the carrier and not one was wrong about the VERDICT -- which is precisely why nothing would ever have re-asked them. The failures were: `run_history.json`, the ANCHOR three rows deferred to, called append-only when it is a whole-list read-modify-write that was measured the same day destroying 100 runs into 1 and publishing the loss as a KPI; `.sent_ntfy_ids.json` and `.ntfy_responder_seen_hashes.json`, called append-only when both write `[-500:]` -- bounded rolling windows that drop the oldest on every write; `.dispatcher_seen.json`, whose `why` said append-only while its own `loader` field said read-modify-write, in the same row; `.staging_watcher_seen.json`, 'same shape as' the sibling it was measurably WORSE than (no `try` at all, on `main()`'s first statement); `.sanity_daemon_last_digest_date`, 'same shape as' a sibling with the OPPOSITE fail direction; and `live_decisions_log.jsonl`, whose 'same reasoning' assumed a repair that had not happened and would have been the WRONG repair here. THE COMMON SHAPE: the resemblance is asserted across exactly the axis on which the carriers differ, because the axis they share is the one the verdict turns on and it is the one the author was looking at. A right verdict on a wrong reason is not a graded row -- the reason is the only part a later reader can check, and `_scope_of_benign`'s RANKING of the loader sweep is computed from it, so a carrier called append-only is filed in the safe half and swept last. A row may cite a sibling to CORROBORATE, never to CONCLUDE: it must first name what its own carrier's writer and reader do.
_verdicts._declassified: OPTIONAL, and the ONLY way a row may stop being a hit without going red. Prose naming the repair that took the path out of the class -- the failure path no longer writes what the alarm reads. It is accepted ONLY when the census can still see the path both WRITTEN and READ: a path with zero writers or zero readers is not a repaired control, it is the derivation having gone blind on it (the 2026-09-05 parameter-seam shape, where run_history.json kept three writers and went to zero readers), and no field excuses that. An empty string or a JSON null is not a reason.
_verdicts._scope_of_the_annotation: EVERY ROW CARRIES A `loader` FIELD, AND `--check` REFUSES A HIT WITHOUT ONE (2026-09-05). `_scope_of_benign` above already said a row with no `loader` 'has not been asked, which is a gap and not a pass' -- and that was prose with no falsifier for exactly as long as it existed. On 2026-09-05 the 34-row loader sweep (`c30738d77`) annotated all 46 rows; nine hours later `9857c0edb`, the resemblance re-audit in the same lane, rewrote this file from a pre-sweep copy and DELETED 33 of those annotations. The merge that carried it to origin (`f7f9d5adc`) was right to adopt the re-audit whole and diffed its resolution against the re-audit's own copy, so the loss was invisible from both sides. Every control was green throughout: `undispositioned()` asks for a verdict and a reason, `unguarded_real_hits()` asks `real` rows for a test, and `eroded_dispositions()` -- the erosion inverse, which landed in the SAME MINUTE as this erosion -- asks whether a ROW still has a HIT, never whether a row still has its ANSWER. `unasked_loader_rows()` is the missing leg: a hit whose row carries no non-empty `loader` is RED, whether it never had one or lost one. Keyed to the property (an unanswered row), not to today's answer.
_verdicts._scope_of_shared_answers: A LOADER ANSWER IS A STATEMENT ABOUT ONE CARRIER'S CODE, SO IT BELONGS ON ONE ROW (2026-09-05 delivery-seat re-audit, the shared-answer pass). `_scope_of_resemblance` one field up caught the reasons that named the sibling they were graded from. It did not catch the same defect at scale and without a name: ONE sentence -- 'ASKED AND CLEAN -- measured across the whole partition (missing/empty/truncated/null/mapping/list-of-ints/bare-string) against a live prior, no state raises and none is a read-modify-write' -- stood verbatim on TWELVE rows. That is worse than 'same shape as X', because it does not LOOK inherited: a row saying 'same shape as X' at least names the row it was graded from, and a bulk sentence names nothing, so nothing marks it as an answer reached once and applied twelve times. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND, by feeding the seven-member partition to each of the twelve loaders: 'no state raises' is TRUE of all twelve. 'None is a read-modify-write' is FALSE of at least three -- `.supervisor_stuck_state.json`, `.atom_stall_tracker.json` and `.product_interleave_state.json` all rewrite the whole record from the loaded one, and are safe for a reason the sentence does not give. And 'ASKED AND CLEAN' answers a DIFFERENT QUESTION from the one `_scope_of_benign` commissioned the field to answer: on 'does the loader tell ABSENT from PRESENT-BUT-UNREADABLE', three of the twelve answer yes, one (`.last_gate_blocking_tests.json`) conflates them with the argument written in its own docstring, and EIGHT conflate them with no argument anywhere. Seven of those eight fail open -- a duplicate page, an extra push, a re-run suite. The eighth, `.reconcile_watch_state.json`, fails QUIET: `[]` is that carrier's clean baseline, so a corrupt state file plus a currently-clean reconcile swallows the drift-RECOVERY page entirely. NO VERDICT MOVED, exactly as in the resemblance pass before it -- which is why nothing would ever have re-asked these rows. TWO MORE were found by the same sweep and are the subtler case: `.seat_continuation.json` and `.weekly_rhythm.json` carried one identical one-line answer, and both were genuinely opened -- but one discriminates at the WRITER and the other at the LOADER, and the shared sentence erased the difference. THE RULE THIS LEAVES: a sentence that appears on two rows is either PROVENANCE (when a row was written, by which pass, under which test) or it is an answer one row did not earn. Provenance is legitimate and is declared in `_shared_provenance`; anything else shared is refused by `shared_loader_answers()`, in writing, the same shape as `declassified` and `_retired` one rung over.

_scope_note: All 6 real hits are GUARDED as of 2026-08-10 (PW2 built the census and guarded .publish_gate_state.json, the instance the steer was about; PW4 chose the close condition for, and guarded, the next four; the sixth, publish_provenance.json, arrived already guarded on 2026-08-10 -- its author reached the once-only-stamp property independently, which is the census working as intended: the class was known before the control was written). Each close condition is NAMED in its own module and INDEPENDENT of the state file it closes (R15 anti-tautology): a pytest pass count, a filesystem-derived work key, the maturity map's own level/stage, a publisher return code. They were deliberately not guarded in one pass -- 'what evidences an episode close' is a per-control judgement, and guarding by reflex with a condition nobody chose produces controls that can never clear, which is the accretion OPERATIONAL_COHERENCE_DESIGN_PASS forbids. `--check` now fails on a `real` row that is not `guarded` with a test citation that exists on disk, so the guard field cannot decay into prose nobody checks.

A 10h26m outage paged as a fresh 14 minutes on 2026-08-09. Guarded via _write_publish_gate_state(episode_closed=...), where the close is evidenced by pending_run_complete_markers()==0. .operational_layer_signal.json.why: `consecutive_red` IS an episode counter and supervisor._operational_red_persistent_draw derives a priority-zero draw from it (>3 consecutive = drawable). run_operational_layer_signal read-modify-writes it, so a check that resolves to green for a reason other than a demonstrated recovery resets the episode the escalation is measured by. CLOSE CONDITION (PW4): rc == 0 AND the run reports >=1 test PASSED -- because pytest exits 0 when every selected test SKIPPED, and the operational marker selects exactly the daemon-lifecycle tests most likely to skip themselves when the daemon they drive is absent (R15 fail-open on empty). Read off the subprocess's own summary line, never off this state file. Guarded via process_run_complete.operational_layer_episode_closed -> _write_operational_layer_state(episode_closed=...). Replay proof: tests/background/test_pw4_episode_guards.py::test_op_a_green_that_ran_nothing_does_not_clear_the_red_episode (and ::test_op_a_real_green_still_clears_it for the opposite direction).

.supervisor_stuck_state.json.why: `first_seen_at` is an episode-start timestamp and _check_stuck_escalation both writes it and reads it to decide escalation. Its episode key was the stuck REASON, and these reasons render counts, levels and elapsed minutes into their prose, so every re-render was a new key: first_seen_at was re-stamped and a long stall read as a series of short ones that never reached the 2h threshold. CLOSE CONDITION (PW4): the reason's NUMBER-AND-PLURAL-normalised form changed, or the evidence _stuck_key already carries changed (agenda updated_at / PRIORITIES.md mtime / the staged set) -- all read off the filesystem and off find_work's live draw, never off this state file. Normalised rather than dropped: dropping the reason would make every draw against the same staging backlog ONE episode and page at work that is genuinely moving. Guarded via supervisor._stuck_episode_key + guard_episode(since_fields=STUCK_SINCE_FIELDS). Replay proof: tests/background/test_pw4_episode_guards.py::test_stuck_a_reworded_reason_does_not_restamp_the_episode (opposite direction: ::test_stuck_genuinely_different_work_still_opens_a_fresh_episode).
.supervisor_stuck_state.json.loader: RE-OPENED 2026-09-05 by the shared-answer re-audit (this row's `loader` was one of twelve carrying ONE verbatim sentence). The seven-member partition was fed to this carrier's own loader and the outcomes below are what it returned. TELLS THEM APART, AND THE CALLER ACTS ON IT -- the best of the twelve alongside `.product_interleave_state.json`. absent -> `({}, 'absent')`; empty/truncated/null/list-of-ints/bare-string -> `({}, 'unreadable')`; `{"a": 1}` -> `({'a': 1}, 'readable')`. Nothing raises. `_check_stuck_escalation` reads the VERDICT, not just the state: `lost = prior_unreadable(prior)` suppresses `episode_closed`, so a corrupt file cannot re-stamp `first_seen_at` and shorten a running stall, and `prior_unreadable` is written INTO the record so the next reader sees a lost memory rather than a new episode. AND THE SHARED SENTENCE WAS WRONG ABOUT THE MECHANISM: it said `none is a read-modify-write`, and `_save_stuck_state(state)` rewrites the WHOLE record from the loaded one -- this carrier is safe BECAUSE of `guard_episode` + `prior_unreadable`, not because there is no read-modify-write. A right answer resting on a false reason is the shape this re-audit exists for.

.atom_stall_tracker.json.why: `consecutive_unchanged` per atom is an episode counter, and _record_atom_draw_and_check_stall writes the same field its own stall check reads. The episode closed on ANY fingerprint difference, and two of the five fingerprint components change without the atom advancing -- an `expert_hour.last` re-stamp (which IS the livelock the tracker exists to catch, resetting the counter meant to catch it) and a `level_target` re-plan. CLOSE CONDITION (PW4): level_current changed, loop_stage changed, or simplifications_count went UP -- the atom's own advancing state in docs/design/maturity_map.yaml, read from the map at draw time and never from this file. Guarded via supervisor._atom_fingerprint_progressed + guard_episode(streak_fields=ATOM_STALL_STREAK_FIELDS). Replay proof: tests/background/test_pw4_episode_guards.py::test_stall_an_expert_hour_restamp_does_not_reset_the_streak (opposite direction: ::test_stall_real_progress_still_closes_the_episode).
.atom_stall_tracker.json.loader: RE-OPENED 2026-09-05 by the shared-answer re-audit (this row's `loader` was one of twelve carrying ONE verbatim sentence). The seven-member partition was fed to this carrier's own loader and the outcomes below are what it returned. TELLS THEM APART, AND THE CALLER ACTS ON IT. Identical outcomes to `.supervisor_stuck_state.json` because both are on `load_episode_prior` -- and that is a measured fact about THIS path, not a resemblance: absent -> `({}, 'absent')`, every unreadable member -> `({}, 'unreadable')`, `{"a": 1}` -> readable, nothing raises. `_record_atom_draw_and_check_stall` takes `lost = prior_unreadable(prior)` at supervisor.py:6369 and stamps `prior_unreadable` into the record, so `consecutive_unchanged` after a lost prior is published as a FLOOR rather than as an episode. `_save_atom_stall_state` IS a whole-record rewrite, so the shared sentence's `none is a read-modify-write` was false here too; the class guard, not the absence of a rewrite, is what holds the streak.

.run_marker_sweep_state.json.why: `cycles` counts consecutive zero-progress sweeps and _check_zero_progress writes the counter its own alarm reads. Its close was implicit and wrong -- 'the oldest marker's NAME changed' -- but retiring a superseded marker is a rename that needs no run lock and cannot be lock-skipped, so it drains the queue whether or not publishing works at all and reset the count on a stall that was still running. CLOSE CONDITION (PW4): a publisher invocation returned rc == 0, recorded by _record_marker_published at the one site that sees it; plus an empty queue, the same independent signal the publish gate's own episode uses. Both are independent of this state file. Narrower than 'the backlog shrank' on purpose: the alarm's claim is that the PUBLISH PATH is not moving, and only a publish refutes it. Replay proof: tests/background/test_pw4_episode_guards.py::test_sweep_a_retirement_does_not_reset_the_zero_progress_count (opposite direction: ::test_sweep_a_publish_closes_the_episode).

publish_provenance.json.why: `paused_since` IS an episode-start timestamp, and it is rendered as the SEVERITY of the loudest alarm surface this machine has -- a public banner reading 'Verification paused since T' (publish_provenance.banner_line, published by process_run_complete._publish_provenance_banner on exactly the cycles the numbers must not move). record_paused is on the gate-RED path and writes the same file that banner reads, so a re-stamp every red cycle would page a 25-hour pause as 'paused since 30 seconds ago' -- the .publish_gate_state.json instance wearing the opposite coat, and on the visitor's page rather than the director's phone. ALREADY GUARDED, and guarded in its own module rather than through background/episode_monotonic.py: record_paused stamps only `if not state.get('paused_since')`, and the sole writer that clears it is record_verified, reachable only from a publish that COMPLETED with the scoped gate green. That close is independent of this file (the publisher's own return path), which is the anti-tautology property the other five real rows are held to. Replay proof: tests/background/test_publish_provenance.py::test_paused_since_is_stamped_once_not_re_stamped_every_cycle (opposite direction: ::test_recovery_clears_the_pause_and_advances). A second, stronger property sits alongside the episode guard and is mutation-proven separately: record_paused cannot write showing_run or last_verified AT ALL, so no failure path can advance the freshness claim -- tests/background/test_publish_provenance.py::test_a_pause_cannot_move_the_served_run_by_a_byte.

.supervisor_idle_turn_count.json.why: `count` is all-time and strictly increasing (_record_idle_turn does _load()+1 and nothing ever resets it). It already HAS the shape this atom's guard enforces, arrived at independently -- a high-water counter cannot be shortened.
.supervisor_idle_turn_count.json.loader: RESTORED 2026-09-05 -- this annotation was DELETED, with 32 others, by `9857c0edb` (the resemblance re-audit in this same lane), which rewrote the whole file from a copy taken before the loader sweep landed. The text below is the sweep's own, restored verbatim from `76665df6e`; nothing in it was re-derived, and nothing in the re-audit contradicted it. ORIGINAL: SWEPT 2026-09-05. `_load_idle_turn_count` was `json.loads(...).get('count', 0)` under `except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError)`, and `null` and `[1, 2, 3]` both parse, so neither reached the except and the `.get` one line later raised AttributeError. WHERE THAT RAISE WENT is the finding: it escapes `run_cycle` -- no try covers the call -- but `main`'s loop catches every Exception, so the supervisor does NOT die. It logs `Supervisor cycle error` every two minutes forever and the tick never completes, which is the responder's alive-and-deaf shape rather than the producer's, and it fires on exactly the branch that exists to make an idle machine visible. The pre-registration predicted the tick would be KILLED; that was half wrong and the correction is recorded beside it in the loader's docstring. The CONFLATION here is deliberately left alone rather than repaired: absent and unreadable both start from 0, the reset is genuinely cheap (`count` is all-time, its only consumers are a log line and `naive_organ`'s evidence reference, and nothing reads it for severity), so this carrier gets the crash fix and NOT an alarm it would have to earn -- guarding by reflex with an escalation nobody chose is what the _scope_note above forbids. A bool `count` is also refused: `isinstance(True, int)` is True, and an accepted bool increments to 2 and makes the all-time total wrong rather than absent. Control: tests/background/test_the_status_board_and_the_idle_counter_survive_a_read_they_cannot_perform.py

.supervisor_map_exhausted_state.json.why: A single boolean edge-detector ({"exhausted": bool}) that fires on the false->true transition (R5). It records no episode start and no streak, so there is no episode length for a failure to shorten. Separately weak -- it can never report HOW LONG the map has been exhausted -- but that is a missing measure, not a self-clearing one.

That is inside the supervisor's own cycle, so `main`'s blanket handler keeps the daemon alive while the tick never completes, every two minutes forever -- the alive-and-deaf shape, on the branch whose entire job is making a stuck machine visible. Same defect as `_load_idle_turn_count`, reached through a different door, which is why the whole partition was swept rather than the instance. Repaired via `load_episode_prior`. The CONFLATION is left: the record is one boolean edge, an unreadable prior costs one duplicate NTFY of an escalation this daemon WANTS sent, and guarding it would be an escalation nobody chose.

.last_tested_hash.why: Written ONLY on a gate PASS, never on a failure, so no failure path touches it. It is load-bearing in the opposite direction: the wedge draw reads it as the INDEPENDENT anti-tautology cross-check (a pass at HEAD means the failures are stale). Changing it to record failures would DESTROY that independence.
